talking_points.headline: Agent access terms underline authorization and liability questions
talking_points.context_html: The report describes Citi’s terms for third-party agents using customer credentials and PNC’s distinction between approved connections and unrestricted access. A control question for banking operations is how consent, permitted actions and transaction records would support investigation when an agent exceeds its mandate. The article notes that consumer liability depends on applicable law and the facts of a transaction.

On Adam's Desk.title: HSBC CEO Sees Deposit Growth and Asian Wealth as Bank Bets on AI
On Adam's Desk.summary: MarketBeat reports that HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery discussed deposit competition, Asian wealth investment, AI use and organizational simplification at a JPMorgan conference; the excerpt gives no publication date. It reports $1.1 trillion in Asian wealth balances and $95 billion in regional net new money during the first nine months of the year, alongside investment to strengthen wealth products and services. The figures and remarks provide competitive context for wealth delivery and process redesign, but the excerpt does not establish implementation detail or a dated event.

Regulatory & Markets.title: MAS explores AI agent protocol and tokenisation framework
Regulatory & Markets.summary: MAS outlined plans for an agent-verification protocol and sandbox for AI agents and programmable money, and released a tokenised-collateral framework covering lifecycle requirements such as eligibility, custody and valuation. This adds a specific operational framework to the previously reported MAS agent and tokenisation agenda; for banking delivery, the collateral lifecycle and agent mandate become concrete control and interoperability questions. The protocol, sandbox and further work remain planned or exploratory rather than established production arrangements.

Regulatory & Markets.title: SFF day two: the money is ready, the agents are not - The Fintech Times
Regulatory & Markets.summary: At the Singapore FinTech Festival, MAS described its tokenised-bill issuance, settlement and further live trials, alongside plans for agent safeguards and a “know your agent” protocol. The article adds that the S$100 million issue drew applications of more than twice the amount offered and is due to mature on 4 December; these details add context to the previously reported issuance, while the article also notes that tokenised-market value remains small relative to conventional markets. For banking delivery, the reported pilots and trials make interoperability, settlement arrangements and controls important dependencies; most cited activity remains testing or planned expansion.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Citi Says Customers Are Responsible When AI Banking Agents Go Rogue—Even After a Hack - Decrypt
Regulatory & Markets.summary: Decrypt reports that Citi revised its online terms to treat activity by third-party AI agents using customer-supplied credentials as customer-authorised, subject to applicable law, while PNC distinguishes approved connections from unrestricted credential sharing. The article also notes uncertainty about how consumer protections apply to agent-initiated transactions and describes other US banks’ warnings or policy changes. For banking operations, the contrast makes authorization evidence, permitted access methods and loss-handling rules key design questions; the legal treatment remains fact-dependent.

Competitor Intelligence.title: DBS Now Enables Large Companies to Issue Digital Vouchers for PayLah!
Competitor Intelligence.summary: DBS has extended its Programmable Rewards service to large companies, with Chubb Insurance Singapore named as its first corporate client; eligible policy customers receive digital vouchers redeemable at authorised NETS merchants through PayLah!. DBS says companies can constrain voucher use and that redemptions are verified automatically, with SME access planned for later phases. For operations, the model depends on clear merchant eligibility and reliable redemption verification; the report does not establish adoption beyond the named initial client.

AI & Technology.title: MAS and SFA Name 11 Winners of 2026 FinTech Awards at Singapore FinTech Festival
AI & Technology.summary: MAS and the Singapore FinTech Association named 11 winners across the 2026 Global FinTech Hackcelerator and SFF FinTech Excellence Awards. The reported solutions include AI for credit and fraud modelling, wealth-advisory drafts routed to relationship managers for approval, and regulatory compliance; finalists may explore pilot engagements with corporate champions. These examples offer signals about emerging capabilities, but awards and pilot opportunities do not establish broad deployment or proven results.
